description:
The /fly HUD speed readout displays 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) once the spacecraft passes ~2.5 AU from the Sun — which happens rapidly on every outer-system flight.

Expected: The HUD speed readout should show a physically plausible heliocentric speed in km/s for any destination, not just Earth→Mars transfers. For a spacecraft on an Earth→Jupiter transfer at Jupiter distance, the speed should be roughly Jupiter's orbital speed (~13 km/s) plus or minus the hyperbolic excess.

Acceptance criteria:
- The HUD speed readout on /fly must display a finite numeric km/s value (not NaN) for every mission destination, including Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto. [code-invariant: NaN is a crash signal — the app must not display NaN in a user-facing HUD readout. Line 6783 renders `heliocentricKms.toFixed(2)`, which produces 'NaN km/s' when heliocentricKms is NaN.]
- The displayed speed must be computed from a transfer semi-major axis appropriate to the actual destination, not hardcoded to the Mars transfer ellipse. [spec: file src/routes/fly/+page.svelte lines 950-952: the second argument to flyHeliocentricSpeed is hardcoded to (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2 ≈ 1.262 AU for all non-Moon missions, regardless of destination. The function doc in src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts line 32-36 explicitly documents aTransferAu as 'transfer-ellipse semi-major axis (AU). For an Earth→Mars Hohmann a ≈ 1.262' — the hardcoded value is the Earth→Mars value and was never generalized.]
- The speed readout must remain finite throughout the entire simulated trajectory, from launch through cruise through arrival. [code-invariant: Line 6783 renders `heliocentricKms.toFixed(2)`. toFixed produces 'NaN' when the value is NaN. The derivation feeds into the rendering path — NaN propagates to the user.]

Domain facts:
- Jupiter semi-major axis ≈ 5.2 AU; Earth→Jupiter Hohmann transfer a ≈ (1 + 5.2)/2 = 3.1 AU
- Saturn semi-major axis ≈ 9.5 AU; Earth→Saturn Hohmann a ≈ 5.25 AU
- Uranus semi-major axis ≈ 19.2 AU; Earth→Uranus Hohmann a ≈ 10.1 AU
- Neptune semi-major axis ≈ 30.1 AU; Earth→Neptune Hohmann a ≈ 15.55 AU
- Pluto semi-major axis ≈ 39.5 AU; Earth→Pluto Hohmann a ≈ 20.25 AU
- Ceres semi-major axis ≈ 2.77 AU; Earth→Ceres Hohmann a ≈ 1.885 AU
